components.name: Alert
components.description:
An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, an action and a dismiss button.
The icon is decorative and a visually hidden prefix names the tone for screen readers.

props.name: tone
props.description: Kind of message: `info` (neutral, default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading of the alert, in one line: what happened. Plain text, not a document heading.

props.name: children
props.description: The detail: why it happened and what to do.

props.name: action
props.description: A single action next to the text, usually a link or a small `Button` ("Update card").

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The alert is removed by the parent.

props.name: urgent
props.description:
The message interrupts the user's task and must be announced immediately (`role="alert"`,
assertive). Use it only for failures the user must know about right now.

props.name: announce
props.description:
Whether the alert is a live region (`role="status"`, polite). Default `true`, because most
alerts appear after something the user did. Set `false` for a static notice that is part
of the page content from the start: it then has no role and is read in page order.
Ignored when `urgent`.

props.name: messages
props.type: Partial<{ dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>
props.description: Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages.

keys.description: Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of alert; color and icon alone cannot.

items.name: Urgent
items.description: Urgent alerts use `role="alert"` and interrupt screen readers. Reserve them for failures that need attention now.

items.name: StaticNotice
items.description: A static notice that is part of the page from the start has no live region role.

items.name: Dismissible
items.description: Tab to the dismiss button, press Enter.

docs.summary: An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, one action and an optional dismiss button.
whenToUse: Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.
whenNotToUse: Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
A field error: use the field's error message.
A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
examples:
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
- Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
- A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=status | alert | none]  (tinted surface, 1px tinted border, radius lg)
  Icon (decorative)  info | success | warning (triangle) | danger
  content
    VisuallyHidden   "Information" | "Success" | "Warning" | "Error"
    title            optional, 14/22, weight 500
    children         13/18, text-2
  actions            action slot · dismiss IconButton
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                                           | Default  | Notes                                                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tone`      | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | `info` is neutral; the others tint border and background                       |
| `title`     | `ReactNode`                                    |          | What happened, one line                                                        |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                    |          | Why, and what to do                                                            |
| `action`    | `ReactNode`                                    |          | One link or small `Button`                                                     |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void`                                   |          | Shows the dismiss button; the parent removes the alert                         |
| `urgent`    | `boolean`                                      | `false`  | `role="alert"` (assertive). Only for failures that need attention now          |
| `announce`  | `boolean`                                      | `true`   | `false` removes the live region role for static notices. Ignored when `urgent` |
| `messages`  | `{ dismiss, info, success, warning, danger }`  |          | Per-instance overrides                                                         |

The vocabulary uses `info` instead of `neutral` for the plain tone, as in the handoff. Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility: role decisions
sections.content:
- **Default `role="status"` (polite).** Most alerts appear after something the user did (submit, import). A status region is announced politely, without stealing focus or interrupting speech. The handoff used `role="alert"` for every `danger` alert, which interrupts for things that are not urgent; urgency is now an explicit `urgent` prop, not a function of the tone.
- **`urgent` gives `role="alert"` (assertive).** Use it for a failure the user must know right now (lost connection, session expired). Avoid more than one at a time.
- **`announce={false}` gives no role.** A notice that is part of the page when it loads (a permanent banner, a form-level note) does not need a live region; screen readers read it in page order. A live region that never changes is noise, and many `status` regions on one page are worse.
- Live regions announce **changes**: for the announcement to work, render the Alert when the event happens and keep the region mounted; do not render it hidden and unhide it.
- **The tone is not only color and icon.** The icon is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden prefix ("Error", "Warning", "Success", "Information", from messages) names the kind of alert for screen readers.
- The **dismiss button** is an `IconButton` named "Dismiss alert" (messages), reachable by Tab and operated with Enter or Space. After dismissing, the parent should move focus somewhere sensible if the alert held it.
- Text contrast on the tinted backgrounds is at least 4.5:1 (checked in the browser test with the real computed colors). The 6% and 30% tints are component tokens (`--ds-alert-*`).
- Forced colors: the browser repaints border and icon with system colors; the icon and the hidden tone prefix still name the tone.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Title: what happened, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Payment declined").
- Text: why and what to do ("The card ending in 4242 was declined. Use another card.").
- The action is a verb plus object ("Update card"), not "Click here".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Icons are bundled Lucide icons, `aria-hidden`, instead of the text glyphs "i", "check" and "!" that screen readers read aloud. Warning and danger have different icons.
- `role` is `status` by default, `alert` only when `urgent`, none with `announce={false}`.
- Dismiss option, visually hidden tone prefix, and `messages` (English and pt-BR).
- The 6% tint and 30% border are tokens instead of inline `color-mix`; the handoff `--radius` (undefined) is `--ds-radius-lg`.
- No `style` prop.

components.name: Avatar
components.description:
A circular photo or initials of a person, in grays (never a color per person). The `name`
drives the initials and the accessible name; a photo that fails to load falls back to the
initials.

props.name: name
props.description:
The person's full name. Drives the initials and the accessible name (`alt` of the photo).
Optional: still used to compute the initials.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Hides the avatar from assistive technology (`alt=""`). Use it when the name is shown next to it.

props.name: src
props.description: URL of the photo. If it fails to load, the initials are shown instead.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 24px, `md` 28px (default), `lg` 40px.

props.name: ring
props.description: Draws a 2px ring in the surface color, to separate overlapping avatars. Default `false`.

docs.summary: A circular photo or the initials of a person, in grays. There is no color per person.
whenToUse: Identify who owns, created or is assigned to something.
Next to a name in a list, a comment or a menu.
whenNotToUse: For a company logo or a product thumbnail: use an image.
For a status: use `Badge`.
examples: Ada Lovelace

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Identify who owns, created or is assigned to something.
- Next to a name in a list, a comment or a menu.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a company logo or a product thumbnail: use an image.
- For a status: use `Badge`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span.root (circle, role="img" + aria-label when it initials)
  img | span[aria-hidden] initials
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                   | Default | Notes                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`               | -       | Required unless `decorative`. Drives the initials and the accessible name              |
| `src`        | `string`               |         | Photo URL. A load error falls back to the initials                                     |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`  | 24, 28 and 40 px (`--ds-avatar-size-*`)                                                |
| `ring`       | `boolean`              | `false` | 2px surface-colored ring, to separate overlapping avatars                              |
| `decorative` | `boolean`              | `false` | Hides the avatar from assistive technology (`alt=""`). Use it next to the visible name |

The type makes `name` required when the avatar is not decorative. Other `span` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Initials
sections.content: `getInitials(name, locale)` (also exported) takes the first letter of the first and of the last word: "Ana Maria da Silva" is `AS`; a single word gives one letter. It uses `Intl.Segmenter` (combined characters stay whole) and `toLocaleUpperCase` with the `DSProvider` locale (`i` becomes `İ` in Turkish). The gray shade is derived from the name, so one person always looks the same.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content: - With initials the root is `role="img"` named by `name`; the letters are `aria-hidden` so they are not read twice. - With a photo the `` has `alt={name}`. A decorative avatar has `alt=""` and no role. - The handoff set `alt` to the initials ("AL"), which is meaningless to a screen reader; the full name is used now. - If the image cannot be loaded the initials appear and the accessible name stays the same. - Avatars are not interactive. Put one inside a button or link that has its own name and mark it `decorative`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Pass the full display name, not the initials.
- Never pass an email or an id as `name`.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: ```tsx Ada Lovelace ``` Stacked avatars: wrap them in a flex container with `role="group"` and an `aria-label`, give each `ring`, and overlap with a negative inline margin. A dedicated `AvatarGroup` is not part of this version.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `name` replaces `initials`; initials are computed and locale-aware.
- `alt` is the person's name, or empty when `decorative`.
- Image error fallback.
- `size` is `sm | md | lg` (tokens) instead of a number; `tone` and `ring` color props are gone (shade is derived from the name, ring is a boolean).
- No `style` prop.

alternatives.reason: For a status: use `Badge`.

components.name: Badge
components.description:
A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the
dot only reinforce it.

props.name: children
props.description: The status text. Required: color and the dot never carry the meaning alone.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Meaning of the badge: `accent` open or in progress, `success` done, `warning` pending,
`danger` failed, `neutral` everything else (default).

props.name: dot
props.description: Shows the small decorative dot before the text. It is hidden from assistive technology. Default `true`.

docs.summary: A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the dot only reinforce it.
whenToUse: Show the state of a record in a list, a table row or a card header: Draft, In progress, Shipped, Failed.
Keep the text short (one to three words, sentence case).
whenNotToUse: For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Show the state of a record in a list, a table row or a card header: Draft, In progress, Shipped, Failed.
- Keep the text short (one to three words, sentence case).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
- For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
- For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
[ dot ] Text
```

- `dot` (optional, decorative, `aria-hidden`).
- `text`: required, the status.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop        | Type                                                          | Default     | Notes                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tone`      | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | `accent` open or in progress, `success` done, `warning` pending, `danger` failed |
| `dot`       | `boolean`                                                     | `true`      | Decorative dot before the text                                                   |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                   | required    | The status text                                                                  |
| `className` | `string`                                                      |             | Merged with the component class                                                  |

Other `span` attributes and `ref` are passed to the root element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A Badge is plain text in a `span`: there is no role and no keyboard behavior.
- The dot is `aria-hidden`; the tone is never the only carrier of meaning, because the text names the status (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Text on every soft tint keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast (checked in the browser test by compositing the real computed colors).
- In forced-colors mode the Badge gets a border and the dot takes the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Sentence case, no punctuation, no emoji: "In progress", not "IN PROGRESS!".
- Name the state, not the action: "Shipped", not "Ship".
- If the status can be unknown, say so with text ("Unknown"), do not omit the Badge.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
<Badge dot={false}>Draft</Badge>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Tones use only the semantic tokens (`--ds-*-soft`). The handoff built the danger tint with a different `color-mix` (14%) than the token (10%); the token is now the single source.
- Height, dot size and padding are component tokens (`--ds-badge-*`).
- The dot is explicitly decorative; `children` is required.
- No `style` prop.

components.name: Button
components.description:
An action button built on React Aria's `Button`.

Use one `primary` button per screen. While `isPending` the button keeps its width, shows a
spinner, stays focusable, sets `aria-disabled` and ignores presses, so it can be explained
by a tooltip and focus is never lost.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual style.
- `primary`: the single main action of the screen (light ink on dark). One per screen.
- `secondary`: default for other actions.
- `ghost`: tertiary, low emphasis actions.
- `danger`: destructive action that is not yet confirmed.
- `danger-solid`: the confirm button of a destructive dialog.

props.name: size
props.description: Height token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the width of the container.

props.name: leading
props.description: Node before the label, usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative; the label names the button.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Node after the label, for example a `Kbd` shortcut hint.

props.name: children
props.description: Label: a short verb plus object in sentence case ("Create order").

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the underlying `<button>` element.

items.name: Primary
items.description: Use one `primary` button per screen, at the top right of the view.

items.name: DangerSolid
items.description: The confirm button of a destructive dialog.

items.name: Pending
items.description: The button keeps its width and stays focusable while pending; presses are ignored.

items.name: LongText
items.description: Long labels wrap instead of overflowing their container.

items.name: Rtl
items.description: Right-to-left layout: icons and labels swap sides through logical properties.

items.name: KeyboardActivation
items.description: Keyboard: Tab focuses, Enter and Space press.

items.name: Focused
items.description: Focus state shown through a play function.

docs.summary:
The control for an action. Built on React Aria's `Button`, styled with tokens and `data-*` state attributes.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/Button` (CMP-FRM-01).
whenToUse: To run an action in place: "Create order", "Mark as shipped".
`danger` for a destructive action that opens a confirmation, `danger-solid` for the confirm button inside that dialog (initial focus stays on Cancel).
`ghost` for low-emphasis actions such as "View all" in a card header.
whenNotToUse: To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
For a two-state toggle: use a toggle component.
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press (RAC). One tab stop.

sections.heading: One primary per screen
sections.content: Use **one `primary` button per screen**, at the top right of the view, ideally with a keyboard shortcut. Primary is "ink for action": light on dark, never the accent color. Every other action is `secondary` or `ghost`. A second primary button means the screen has two main jobs: split the screen or demote one action.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- To run an action in place: "Create order", "Mark as shipped".
- `danger` for a destructive action that opens a confirmation, `danger-solid` for the confirm button inside that dialog (initial focus stays on Cancel).
- `ghost` for low-emphasis actions such as "View all" in a card header.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
- For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
- For a two-state toggle: use a toggle component.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: `[leading] label [trailing]` inside one native `<button>`. When pending, the content keeps its box (invisible) and a `Spinner` is centered on top, so the width never changes.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                                                                | Default       | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`    | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger' \| 'danger-solid'` | `'secondary'` | See above.                                                                                |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'`                                              | `'md'`        | 32, 40, 48 px (`--ds-control-h-*`). Taller if the label wraps.                            |
| `fullWidth`  | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Fills the container.                                                                      |
| `leading`    | `ReactNode`                                                         | none          | Usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative.                                                 |
| `trailing`   | `ReactNode`                                                         | none          | For example a shortcut hint in mono.                                                      |
| `isPending`  | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Busy: spinner, `aria-disabled`, presses and form submission ignored, stays focusable.     |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                                                           | `false`       | Native `disabled`: not focusable, 35% opacity.                                            |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`                                           | none          | React Aria press event (mouse, touch, keyboard, screen reader). Prefer it over `onClick`. |
| `type`       | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'`                                   | `'button'`    | Stays `button` so a button never submits a form by accident.                              |
| `className`  | `string`                                                            | none          | Merged with the component class.                                                          |

Other React Aria `Button` props (`form*`, `autoFocus`, `aria-*`, `onHoverStart`, ...) and `ref` pass through. `style` and render-prop children are not accepted.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A real `<button>`; the name is its visible label.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press (RAC). One tab stop.
- Focus: accent border plus a 3px ring through `data-focus-visible`, a transparent outline that forced-colors mode repaints as `Highlight`. Mouse clicks do not show the ring.
- Pending: the button stays in the tab order (focus is not lost while waiting) with `aria-disabled="true"` (React Aria does not set `aria-busy`). React Aria announces the busy state when the focused button becomes pending and again when it finishes. The spinner is named "Loading" (pt-BR "Carregando", from the `Spinner` messages) and sits inside the button so it is part of the button's content.
- Disabled: removed from the tab order. Explain _why_ in nearby text rather than relying on a disabled button alone.
- Targets: at least 32px high, above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8.
- Contrast: label colors meet 4.5:1 on their backgrounds in every variant; disabled controls are exempt.
- Reduced motion: the only transition is a 150ms background color change, which the global reduced-motion rule neutralizes. The pending spinner turns into a static ring.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Verb plus object, sentence case: "Create order", "Retry charge". Never a bare "OK" or "Send".
- Destructive buttons name the action: "Delete order".
- No exclamation marks, no emoji, no decorative ellipsis. Use "..." only when the action opens something that needs more input ("Move to...").

sections.heading: States
sections.content: Hover (one surface step lighter; primary dims with `--ds-button-hover-brightness`), focus-visible, disabled, pending. Hover, focus and pending are CSS (`data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-pending`), never React state. There is no press animation.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: ```tsx ```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Hover is CSS, not JS state.
- `isPending` replaces the "disabled plus spinner in leading" recipe: width-stable, focusable, announced, and it ignores presses.
- Sizes are 32 / 40 / 48 px. The handoff `Button.prompt.md` said 28 / 32 / 40; the code and the tokens win.
- `onPress` (React Aria) is the primary event; `disabled` is now `isDisabled`.
- `style` was removed; the primary hover brightness (0.88) and the danger-solid one (0.9) are component tokens.
- Wrapping instead of `white-space: nowrap`, so long labels never overflow.

components.name: Card
components.description:
A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region
(`section` named by its heading).

props.name: title
props.description:
Title shown as an uppercase mono caption. It is a real heading (see `headingLevel`) and
names the card region through `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls placed at the end of the header, next to the title (buttons, a menu).

props.name: variant
props.description:
`default` is a flat surface with a border. `raised` uses the raised surface, a stronger
border and the overlay shadow: use it only for a card that floats above the page (a
pinned panel, a detail popover shell), never for cards that sit in the normal flow.

props.name: padding
props.description: `md` applies the card padding token; `none` removes it (for full-bleed content such as a table). Default `md`.

docs.summary: A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region.
whenToUse: Group a set of related fields, numbers or a list under one caption.
Put page sections side by side in a grid.
whenNotToUse: To wrap a whole page: use the page layout.
For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.
Do not nest a Card inside a Card; use a divider instead.
examples:
<Card title="Storage" actions={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>}>
  <Progress value={62} label="Used" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" />
</Card>

<Card title="Details" headingLevel={3}>…</Card>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Group a set of related fields, numbers or a list under one caption.
- Put page sections side by side in a grid.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To wrap a whole page: use the page layout.
- For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.
- Do not nest a Card inside a Card; use a divider instead.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
section (surface + 1px line, radius lg, padding)
  header (optional)
    h{headingLevel}  mono caption, uppercase by CSS
    actions          optional controls
  children
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop           | Type                         | Default     | Notes                                                                    |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`        | `ReactNode`                  |             | Rendered as a heading styled as a mono caption                           |
| `headingLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2`         | Pick the level that fits the page outline                                |
| `actions`      | `ReactNode`                  |             | End of the header                                                        |
| `variant`      | `'default' \| 'raised'`      | `'default'` | `raised` only for a card that floats above the page                      |
| `padding`      | `'md' \| 'none'`             | `'md'`      | `none` for full-bleed content such as a table (the header keeps padding) |

Other `section` attributes (including `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`) and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Elevation
sections.content: Borders carry hierarchy, shadows are for overlays (AGENTS.md section 5). A `raised` card gets the raised surface, a stronger border **and** `--ds-shadow-overlay`, so use it only when the card really floats (a pinned side panel, the shell of a custom popover). A card in the normal flow stays `default`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The root is a `section`. With a `title`, the heading id is wired to `aria-labelledby`, so screen readers expose a named `region` landmark. Without a title or a label it is a plain generic container (no landmark), which is correct for decorative grouping.
- Give a title-less card an `aria-label` when it should be a landmark.

- The caption uses `--ds-text-2` (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`, which drops below 4.5:1 on the raised surface).

sections.content:
- Captions are sentence case in the source ("Storage"); uppercase is applied by CSS only.
- Keep captions to one to three words.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Card title="Storage" actions={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>}>
  <Progress value={62} label="Used" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" />
</Card>

<Card title="Details" headingLevel={3}>…</Card>
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                      | Notes                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`                                                   | Visible label. Without it pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise).         |
| `description`                                             | Secondary text under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.              |
| `errorMessage`                                            | Error for a single checkbox (for example a required agreement). In a group, set it on the group. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)` | React Aria naming for controlled and uncontrolled use.                                           |
| `isIndeterminate`                                         | Shows a minus; the native input is `indeterminate` until toggled.                                |
| `name`, `value`                                           | Submitted with the form while checked (`value` defaults to `on`).                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`     | Standard states.                                                                                 |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                        | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                               |

`CheckboxGroup` takes `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`, `orientation` (`vertical` default, `horizontal`), `name`, `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange(values: string[])`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`. Each child `Checkbox` needs a `value`.

sections.content:
- 18px box, radius from `--ds-checkbox-radius` (5px), `--ds-line-control` border (3:1 or better in every state), accent fill with a `--ds-text-inverse` check when selected, minus when indeterminate.
- Hover brightens the border; it never changes the fill.
- The whole row is the click target and is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8).
- A disabled group dims once as a whole; disabled single checkboxes use `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Space toggles the focused checkbox. Tab moves between checkboxes; each checkbox is a tab stop.
- Name comes from the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- Group: `role="group"` named by the label, with the group description and error.
- Forced colors: borders and the check glyph use system colors; the glyph (check or minus) carries the state.

<Checkbox label="I accept the terms" name="terms" isRequired errorMessage="Accept the terms to continue." />

<CheckboxGroup label="Notify me about" name="topics" defaultValue={['orders']}>
  <Checkbox value="orders" label="New orders" />
  <Checkbox value="stock" label="Low stock" description="When a fabric drops below its minimum." />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

docs.summary: A typographic placeholder for a list, table or panel that has nothing to show. It says what happened and what the user can do about it.
whenToUse: A list, table or search has no results.
A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.
whenNotToUse: While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.
examples:
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- A list, table or search has no results.
- A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
- For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div.root (dashed border, centered)
  span[aria-hidden]  icon (optional)
  h{headingLevel}    title
  p                  description (optional)
  div                secondaryAction, action
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop              | Type                         | Default | Notes                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`           | `ReactNode`                  | -       | What happened. Rendered as a heading                               |
| `headingLevel`    | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2`     | Match the page outline (inside a `Card` titled with `h2`, use `3`) |
| `description`     | `ReactNode`                  |         | What to do next. Max width 360 px                                  |
| `icon`            | `ReactNode`                  |         | Optional, decorative. No illustrations                             |
| `action`          | `ReactNode`                  |         | Primary action (usually `Button`)                                  |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode`                  |         | Lower emphasis; shown before the primary action                    |
| `compact`         | `boolean`                    | `false` | Less padding, smaller title. For cards, panels, table bodies       |
| `bordered`        | `boolean`                    | `true`  | Dashed border. Turn off inside an already bordered container       |

Other `div` attributes and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Copy: what happened + what to do
sections.content:
Title: say what is missing, in sentence case, without apologies or exclamation marks. Description: tell the user the next step, in one sentence.

| Situation        | Title             | Description                                              | Action        |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Filtered to zero | No orders found   | Try another filter or search term.                       | Clear filters |
| First use        | No orders yet     | Orders created here or in the store appear in this list. | Create order  |
| Cleared inbox    | Nothing to review | New approvals appear here as they arrive.                | (none)        |

Avoid "Oops", "Sorry", blame ("You have no orders") and filler ("There is nothing to show here at the moment").

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The title is a real heading: choose `headingLevel` so the outline stays sequential. The heading lets screen reader users find the empty region by navigating headings.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the text carries the meaning.
- The component does not announce itself. If the empty state replaces content after a user action (for example a search), announce the result count in your own live region.
- Actions are ordinary buttons or links with their own names; order in the DOM is secondary then primary, matching the visual order.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />
```

sections.content:
- The title is a heading (`<h2>` by default) instead of a `span`; the level is configurable.
- Optional decorative `icon` slot (no illustrations, per the visual foundations).
- The handoff Portuguese sample copy is gone; the guidance above replaces it.
- Padding, description width and the compact padding are component tokens (`--ds-empty-state-*`). No `style` prop.

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. ```tsx

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

docs.summary:
An inline SVG icon from the curated Lucide set. It inherits the text color, draws a 1.5px stroke and is hidden from assistive technology unless you give it a `label`.

- Replaces: the runtime `unpkg.com/lucide-static` CSS-mask loading (ICON-001), text glyphs used as icons (ICON-002) and the ad hoc icon rules (ICON-003).
- Built on: `lucide-react`, bundled and tree-shakeable. No network access, no CDN.
whenToUse: Next to a text label to reinforce it (button leading slot, menu item, alert, input affordance).
Inside `IconButton`, which supplies the accessible name.
On its own only when it carries meaning that no nearby text states. Then set `label`.
whenNotToUse: As the only carrier of meaning or status. Color and shape never replace text.
For filled, colored or multi-color icons, emoji or Unicode glyphs. Use the set below.
For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
For an icon that is not in the set. Add it to `icons.ts` with a documented use first.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Next to a text label to reinforce it (button leading slot, menu item, alert, input affordance).
- Inside `IconButton`, which supplies the accessible name.
- On its own only when it carries meaning that no nearby text states. Then set `label`.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- As the only carrier of meaning or status. Color and shape never replace text.
- For filled, colored or multi-color icons, emoji or Unicode glyphs. Use the set below.
- For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
- For an icon that is not in the set. Add it to `icons.ts` with a documented use first.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: A single `<svg>` (24x24 viewBox) with a `currentColor` stroke and no fill. Size and stroke come from tokens: `--ds-icon-xs|sm|md|lg` and `--ds-icon-stroke-width`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop          | Type                           | Default | Notes                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `icon`        | `IconComponent` (required)     | none    | One of the exports of the set, such as `SearchIcon`.                       |
| `size`        | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`  | 12, 14, 18, 20 px. Inside buttons use `sm`.                                |
| `label`       | `string`                       | none    | Makes the icon `role="img"` with this name. Without it the icon is hidden. |
| `directional` | `boolean`                      | `false` | Mirrors the icon in RTL. Set it for chevrons and arrows.                   |
| `className`   | `string`                       | none    | Merged with the component class.                                           |

Other SVG attributes and `ref` pass through to the `<svg>`.

sections.heading: The curated set
sections.content:
Import icons from the package, not from `lucide-react`: `import { Icon, SearchIcon } from '@loui/ds'`.

`iconSet` maps the kebab-case names below to the components and `iconNames` documents the use of each. Both are the source of the allow-list in the manifest (AI-002).

arrow-down, arrow-left, arrow-right, arrow-up, calendar, check, chevron-down, chevron-left, chevron-right, chevron-up, chevrons-up-down, circle-alert, circle-check, circle-x, ellipsis, external-link, info, loader, minus, plus, search, star, triangle-alert, x.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Decorative by default: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`.
- With `label`: `role="img"` and `aria-label`. Use short, specific names ("Saved", not "check icon").
- An icon inside a control never names the control. Put the name on the control (`IconButton label`).
- Forced colors: the stroke is `currentColor`, so it follows the system text color.
- Contrast: icons that convey meaning need 3:1 against their background (WCAG 1.4.11).
- Reduced motion: icons do not animate.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are sentence case and describe the meaning ("Saved"), never the picture ("Green check").
- No emoji or text glyphs as icons (AGENTS.md section 7).

Differences from the handoff

- Bundled SVG instead of `unpkg.com/lucide-static@0.400.0` loaded through CSS `mask` at runtime.
- Decorative by default; `label` is the only way to expose an icon.

Label *                          required marker (aria-hidden)
[ leading  value / placeholder  trailing ]
Description
Error
```

sections.heading: Props (key ones)

| Prop                                                                | Notes                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                             | Visible label. Without it you must pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise). |
| `description`                                                       | Helper text (handoff `hint`).                                                                     |
| `errorMessage`                                                      | Error text (handoff `error`), node or function of the validation result. Needs an invalid state.  |
| `isInvalid` / `isRequired` / `isReadOnly` / `isDisabled`            | Standard states. `isInvalid` shows the error at once.                                             |
| `size`                                                              | `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.                                                        |
| `mono`                                                              | Geist Mono with tabular figures.                                                                  |
| `leading` / `trailing`                                              | Adornments inside the box: an `Icon`, a unit, a `Kbd` hint, an `IconButton`.                      |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                        | Controlled and uncontrolled, React Aria naming (`onChange` receives the string, not the event).   |
| `name`, `type`, `autoComplete`, `inputMode`, `maxLength`, `pattern` | Passed to the `<input>`; `name` and the value take part in form submission.                       |
| `validate`, `validationBehavior`                                    | See Field.md.                                                                                     |

- Keyboard: standard text editing. `Enter` submits the surrounding form. Focus is visible as the accent border plus ring; in forced-colors mode it is a system outline.
- The placeholder never replaces the label.
- Click anywhere in the box (including padding) focuses the input. Clicking a decorative adornment does not; make interactive adornments real buttons with their own names.

- Description: one short sentence, no exclamation marks.

- `hint` is `description`, `error` is `errorMessage`; the error is only shown for an invalid field.
- Ids are generated; `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `required` and `readOnly` are wired.

docs.summary: A keyboard shortcut hint in mono type. It renders a real `<kbd>` element.
whenToUse: Next to a command, menu item or button to show its shortcut: "Search `Ctrl K`".
In help text and tooltips that name a key.
whenNotToUse: To register the shortcut: use `useHotkey`. `Kbd` only displays it.
For code or file names: use `<code>`.
keyboard: When the visible text already is the name (`Enter`, `Tab`) nothing is duplicated.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- Next to a command, menu item or button to show its shortcut: "Search `Ctrl K`".
- In help text and tooltips that name a key.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To register the shortcut: use `useHotkey`. `Kbd` only displays it.
- For code or file names: use `<code>`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
kbd.root (border, mono)
  kbd.key   symbol or text   (aria-hidden when a spoken name replaces it)
            VisuallyHidden   spoken name ("Command")
  kbd.key   K
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop       | Type                       | Default  | Notes                                                                     |
| ---------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keys`     | `readonly string[]`        | -        | The keys of one shortcut, in order (`['Mod', 'K']`). Use this or children |
| `children` | `ReactNode`                | -        | Free content shown as is. No accessible expansion                         |
| `platform` | `'apple' \| 'other'`       | detected | Forces how `Mod` and the modifier symbols render (tests, docs)            |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ name; label }>` |          | Overrides the spoken names (`name(key)`) and short labels (`label(key)`)  |

Recognized names in `keys` (case-insensitive): `Mod`, `Cmd`/`Meta`, `Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`/`Option`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Space`, `Up`/`ArrowUp` (and Down, Left, Right), `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`. Anything else (`K`, `/`, `1`) is shown as typed; single letters are upper-cased with the active locale.

sections.heading: Platform awareness
sections.content:
`Mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Control elsewhere. The server and the first client render use `other` (Ctrl) so hydration matches; the component then reads the real platform (`useSyncExternalStore`) and re-renders with the command symbol on Apple devices. Pass `platform` to pin it. The same detection backs `useHotkey`, so the hint always matches the key that works.

On Apple platforms modifiers use symbols (`⌘ ⌃ ⇧ ⌥ ↵ ⎋ ⇥ ⌫ ⌦`); elsewhere they are short text (`Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Esc`, `Del`). Command and the arrows use their symbol everywhere.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Screen readers do not reliably read symbols such as `⌘`. Every symbol or abbreviation is `aria-hidden` and followed by a visually hidden spoken name from the message catalog: "Command K", "Control Shift Escape".
- When the visible text already is the name (`Enter`, `Tab`) nothing is duplicated.
- The element has no role and is not focusable: it is text. The shortcut itself must be announced where it works (for example `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control, which is the control's responsibility).
- Text is `--ds-text-2`, which keeps at least 4.5:1 on the surface (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`).

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Write the logical key (`Mod`), not the platform one.
- One `Kbd` per shortcut. A sequence ("G then I") is two `Kbd`s with the word between them from your own copy; sequences are not a built-in prop.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Kbd keys={['Mod', 'K']} />
<Kbd keys={['Shift', 'Enter']} />
<Kbd keys={['Esc']} />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `keys` replaces hand-typed `⌘K`; the platform decides the modifier.
- Symbols are expanded for assistive technology with messages (English and pt-BR shipped).
- Height and padding are tokens (`--ds-kbd-*`). No `style` prop.

components.description:
The visible label of a field. Must be rendered inside a React Aria field (TextField, Select,
CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, ...), which wires `for` / `aria-labelledby`.
With `isRequired` it appends a visible marker (text from messages) that is hidden from
assistive technology: screen readers get "required" from the control itself (`required` /
`aria-required`), so announcing the marker too would repeat it.

props.description: Adds the required marker after the text. The control itself must also be required.

props.name: messages
props.description: Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`).

Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

docs.summary:
A link to another page, section or site. Built on React Aria's `Link`: a real `<a href>` that uses the router set on `DSProvider` for client-side navigation.

- Handoff source: none (the handoff only had underlined `<a>` styles); part of GAP-002.
whenToUse: To go somewhere: another route, a section (`#id`), a document or an external site.
Inside running text (`inline`), or as a quiet navigation line such as "View all orders" (`standalone`).
whenNotToUse: To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
For a styled call to action that happens to navigate: still a link semantically, but use a `Button` with `href` when it is the primary action of the screen (planned with the button-as-link variant).
keyboard: Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` follows. (`Space` does not activate a link, by design.)
examples:
Read the pricing details before you change a plan.

View all orders Documentation

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- To go somewhere: another route, a section (`#id`), a document or an external site.
- Inside running text (`inline`), or as a quiet navigation line such as "View all orders" (`standalone`).

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
- For a styled call to action that happens to navigate: still a link semantically, but use a `Button` with `href` when it is the primary action of the screen (planned with the button-as-link variant).

sections.heading: Variants
sections.content:
| Variant      | At rest   | Hover and keyboard focus | Use                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inline`     | underline | thicker underline        | Links inside sentences. Default.                                         |
| `standalone` | none      | underline                | Navigation lists, "View all" lines. Only where context makes it obvious. |

Color alone never identifies a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so inline links are always underlined. The accent color (`--ds-accent`) is reserved for focus, selection and links.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                         | Default    | Notes                                                                       |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`       | `string`                     | none       | Destination. Without it the element is a non-navigating `role="link"` span. |
| `variant`    | `'inline' \| 'standalone'`   | `'inline'` | See above.                                                                  |
| `target`     | `string`                     | none       | `_blank` adds `rel`, the icon and the screen reader note.                   |
| `rel`        | `string`                     | none       | Merged with `noopener noreferrer` for `_blank`.                             |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`                    | `false`    | `aria-disabled`, 35% opacity, presses ignored.                              |
| `onPress`    | `(e: PressEvent) => void`    | none       | React Aria press event, fired before navigation.                            |
| `messages`   | `{ opensInNewTab?: string }` | none       | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                   |
| `className`  | `string`                     | none       | Merged with the component class.                                            |

Other React Aria `Link` props (`download`, `routerOptions`, `hrefLang`, `aria-*`, ...) and `ref` pass through.

sections.heading: Routing
sections.content: Wrap the app once: `<DSProvider navigate={router.push} useHref={router.resolve}>`. Links with a relative `href` then navigate without a page reload; modified clicks (Ctrl/Cmd, middle button) and `target="_blank"` keep the browser behavior.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Real `<a href>`: opens in a new tab with the context menu, can be copied, works without JavaScript.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` follows. (`Space` does not activate a link, by design.)
- Focus: 3px accent ring through `data-focus-visible`; forced-colors mode repaints the transparent outline and system link colors apply.
- Links that open a new tab: the name ends with "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers (hidden text from the `Link` messages) and a decorative icon shows it visually. `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is added automatically.
- Contrast: accent `#8AB4FF` on the dark surfaces is well above 4.5:1.
- Target size: inline links in text are exempt from WCAG 2.5.8; standalone links should sit in a 24px-high row.
- Reduced motion: hover changes decoration thickness only, no animation.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Link text describes the destination or action and makes sense out of context: "Pricing details", "Download invoice". Never "click here" or "read more".
- Sentence case, no trailing punctuation inside the link, no emoji.
- Do not repeat the word "link". The role is announced.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx

Read the pricing details before you change a plan.

View all orders Documentation ```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- New component (GAP-002 part); there was no handoff `Link`. Unstyled `<a>` underlines in the handoff foundation are now this component.
- Adds the external-link behavior (`rel`, icon, screen reader note) and a standalone variant.
