components.name: Meter
components.description:
A bar that shows a quantity within a known range (disk used, quota, score), as opposed to
progress of a task. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"`).

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label, wired to the bar with `aria-labelledby`. Required unless you set `aria-label`
or `aria-labelledby`: a bar without a name is an accessibility bug (React Aria warns in development).

props.name: meta
props.description:
Text on the right of the label, in mono type: "6.2 / 10 GB". It is visual only. If it says
more than the percentage, also pass `valueLabel` so screen readers hear the same thing.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the formatted percentage (`62%`, from `Intl` with the active locale) as `meta` when `meta` is not given.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color of the fill. Color is never the only signal: pair it with a label or `meta`. Default `accent`.

docs.summary: A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.
whenToUse: `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
`Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.
whenNotToUse: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.
examples:
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
- `Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                            | Type                                             | Default    | Notes                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                         | `number`                                         | `0`        | Clamped to the range                                                                               |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`          | `number`                                         | `0`, `100` |                                                                                                    |
| `isIndeterminate`               | `boolean` (`Progress` only)                      |            | No `aria-valuenow`; the fill sweeps                                                                |
| `label`                         | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visible label, wired as the accessible name                                                        |
| `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                         |            | Use when there is no visible label. One of the three is required (React Aria warns in development) |
| `meta`                          | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visual text on the right ("6.2 / 10 GB")                                                           |
| `showValue`                     | `boolean`                                        | `false`    | Shows the formatted percentage as `meta`; hidden when indeterminate                                |
| `valueLabel`                    | `ReactNode`                                      |            | The spoken value (`aria-valuetext`). Pass it when `meta` says more than a percentage               |
| `formatOptions`                 | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                       | percent    | Formatting of the automatic value text                                                             |
| `tone`                          | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'accent'` | Fill color                                                                                         |

Other React Aria props, `className` and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff

- Built on React Aria: `role`, name, `aria-valuetext` and the label wiring come from it. The handoff `div role="progressbar"` had no name.
- Indeterminate mode, `valueLabel`, `showValue` and `Meter` are new.
- Width changes use the motion tokens and are disabled under reduced motion. Height and sweep settings are component tokens (`--ds-progress-*`).
- `Progress` no longer takes a `style` prop.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop                            | Type                                             | Default    | Notes                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                         | `number`                                         | `0`        | Clamped to the range                                                                               |
| `minValue`, `maxValue`          | `number`                                         | `0`, `100` |                                                                                                    |
| `isIndeterminate`               | `boolean` (`Progress` only)                      |            | No `aria-valuenow`; the fill sweeps                                                                |
| `label`                         | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visible label, wired as the accessible name                                                        |
| `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` | `string`                                         |            | Use when there is no visible label. One of the three is required (React Aria warns in development) |
| `meta`                          | `ReactNode`                                      |            | Visual text on the right ("6.2 / 10 GB")                                                           |
| `showValue`                     | `boolean`                                        | `false`    | Shows the formatted percentage as `meta`; hidden when indeterminate                                |
| `valueLabel`                    | `ReactNode`                                      |            | The spoken value (`aria-valuetext`). Pass it when `meta` says more than a percentage               |
| `formatOptions`                 | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                       | percent    | Formatting of the automatic value text                                                             |
| `tone`                          | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'accent'` | Fill color                                                                                         |

Other React Aria props, `className` and `ref` go to the root.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Built on React Aria: `role`, name, `aria-valuetext` and the label wiring come from it. The handoff `div role="progressbar"` had no name.
- Indeterminate mode, `valueLabel`, `showValue` and `Meter` are new.
- Width changes use the motion tokens and are disabled under reduced motion. Height and sweep settings are component tokens (`--ds-progress-*`).
- `Progress` no longer takes a `style` prop.

items.name: Anatomy
items.description: The building blocks composed by hand inside a React Aria field. Prefer the ready-made fields.

items.name: ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt

Validation timing: native validation (the default) keeps every error hidden until the first
save attempt, then focuses the first invalid field.

items.name: RealtimeValidation
items.description: The alternative: `validationBehavior="aria"` reports problems while the user types. Use sparingly.

docs.summary:
Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

sections.heading: Exports
sections.content:
| Export | What it is | | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Label` | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker. | | `Description` | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`. | | `FieldError` | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. | | `FieldMessages` | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box. | | `RequiredMark` | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`. | | `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel` | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel

` helps type stories. | | `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result). |

sections.heading: Anatomy and spacing
sections.content:
```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

sections.heading: One state model (ARCH-009)
sections.content:
| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

sections.heading: Required marker
sections.content:
`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

sections.heading: Validation behavior: native (default), and why
sections.content:
React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- Ids come from React Aria (`useId`), not from the label text.
- Error and hint are both shown (see above), and both are programmatically linked.
- One disabled opacity for every control (`--ds-opacity-disabled`); the handoff used per-control values.
- No hover background on fields: hover brightens the border.

whenNotToUse: 2 to 4 options that users compare: `RadioGroup` (or a segmented control).
Typing to filter a long list: `ComboBox` (planned).

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                            | Notes                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`          | As in `Input`.                                                                                      |
| `options`                                       | `SelectOption[]` (`value`, `label`, `isDisabled`) or groups `{ id, label, options }`, mixed freely. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`    | The selected option `value`; `null` means nothing selected. `onChange` receives `string \| null`.   |
| `placeholder`                                   | Trigger text while empty. Default from messages: "Select an option" (pt-BR "Selecione uma opção").  |
| `size`                                          | `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.                                                          |
| `name`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled` | Standard. `name` is submitted through the hidden `<select>`.                                        |
| `popoverClassName`, `className`, `ref`          | Styling hooks; `ref` is the field root.                                                             |
| `messages`                                      | `placeholder`, `requiredMark`.                                                                      |

Option order is yours: the component never reorders. The product rule that lists are alphabetical by default applies to what you pass in: use `sortByText(options, (o) => o.label, locale)` from `@loui/ds` (locale- and accent-aware) unless the order carries meaning (sizes, steps).

sections.heading: Anatomy and styling
sections.content:
- Trigger: the same box as `Input` (`--ds-line-control` border, focus ring, no hover fill), with a chevron.
- Popover: raised surface, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, radius `lg`, layer `--ds-z-dropdown`, at least as wide as the trigger, scrolls above `--ds-select-popover-max-height`.
- Option: `--ds-item-h` (36px) tall, hover and keyboard focus use `--ds-surface-hover`, the selected option shows a check (`Icon`), disabled options use the shared opacity.
- Section captions are mono, uppercase by CSS, in `--ds-text-2` (`--ds-text-3` fails contrast on the raised surface).

sections.heading: Accessibility and keyboard
sections.content:
| Key                                      | Behavior                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | Open the list and focus the selected (or first/last) option    |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`                  | Next / previous enabled option                                 |
| `Home` / `End`                           | First / last option                                            |
| Letters                                  | Typeahead: focus the option starting with what you type        |
| `Enter` / `Space`                        | Select the focused option, close, focus returns to the trigger |
| `Escape`                                 | Close without changing; focus returns to the trigger           |
| Typing on the closed trigger             | Selects by prefix without opening                              |

The trigger is a `button` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, named by the label and described by the description and error. Options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; sections are `role="group"` named by their caption; disabled options have `aria-disabled`.

```tsx
<Select
  label="Region"
  name="region"
  options={[
    { value: 'eu', label: 'EU: Frankfurt' },
    { value: 'us', label: 'US: Virginia' },
  ]}
  isRequired
  errorMessage="Choose a region."
/>
```

- A custom accessible listbox replaces the native `<select>` (ADR-0001), with a hidden native select kept for forms and autofill. This resolves the "native or custom" question of CMP-FRM-05.
- Label association, description, error, `aria-invalid`, required, placeholder and groups are new; handoff `onChange(value, event)` is `onChange(value)`.
- No inline chevron data URI; the chevron is an `Icon` using the icon set.

props.description: Height of the block, or of each line: a number in px or any CSS length. Default `12px` (`--ds-skeleton-height`).

props.name: circle

docs.summary: A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading: a block, a circle, or a few text lines.
whenToUse: The layout of the content is known (a list of rows, a card, an avatar next to text) and the wait is short.
Keep the page from jumping when the data arrives.
whenNotToUse: For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.
For a measurable task: use `Progress`.
When there is nothing to show after loading: use `EmptyState`.
examples:
<section aria-busy={isLoading} aria-label="Recent orders">
  {isLoading ? (
    <>
      <Skeleton circle height={28} />
      <Skeleton lines={3} />
    </>
  ) : (
    <OrderList orders={orders} />
  )}
</section>

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content:
- The layout of the content is known (a list of rows, a card, an avatar next to text) and the wait is short.
- Keep the page from jumping when the data arrives.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- For an action in progress (saving, sending): use `Spinner` or a loading `Button`.
- For a measurable task: use `Progress`.
- When there is nothing to show after loading: use `EmptyState`.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content:
```
span[aria-hidden="true"]  block | circle
span[aria-hidden="true"]  lines → n × span (last one is 60% wide)
```

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop     | Type               | Default | Notes                                                             |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `width`  | `number \| string` | `100%`  | Number is px. Ignored with `circle`                               |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `12px`  | Height of the block or of each line (`--ds-skeleton-height`)      |
| `circle` | `boolean`          | `false` | Diameter is `height`                                              |
| `lines`  | `number`           |         | Text lines; the last is shorter (not when there is only one line) |

sections.content:
- Every skeleton is `aria-hidden="true"`: it is decoration and has no text.

- The pulse (opacity only) is switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. In forced-colors mode the placeholder gets a border because background colors are dropped.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Match the final layout: the same number of rows and similar widths, so nothing moves when the data arrives.
- Show at most one screenful of placeholders.

sections.heading: Examples

<section aria-busy={isLoading} aria-label="Recent orders">

    <>
      <Skeleton circle height={28} />
      <Skeleton lines={3} />
    </>

    <OrderList orders={orders} />

</section>

docs.summary:
An indeterminate loading ring that inherits the text color. Small, quiet, and not a live region.

- Handoff source: `components/feedback/Spinner` (CMP-FBK-06).
- Built on: a plain element with `role="progressbar"`. A pending `Button` wires it as its busy label through React Aria.
whenToUse: Inside a pending `Button` (`isPending`), which renders it for you.
Next to a short status text for a small, bounded wait ("Saving changes").
A single small area that is loading and has no better placeholder.
whenNotToUse: For large areas or page loads: use `Skeleton` so the layout does not jump.
When you know the progress: use `Progress` with a value.

sections.heading: Anatomy
sections.content: One element: a ring with an open top edge. Size comes from `--ds-icon-sm|md|lg`, thickness from `--ds-spinner-stroke-width`, rotation time from `--ds-spinner-duration`.

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
| Prop         | Type                   | Default   | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`       | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`    | 14, 18, 20 px. Use `sm` inside `sm` and `md` buttons.                                     |
| `label`      | `string`               | "Loading" | Accessible name. Say what is loading when it helps ("Loading orders").                    |
| `decorative` | `boolean`              | `false`   | Hides the spinner from assistive technology. Only when other UI announces the busy state. |
| `messages`   | `{ loading?: string }` | none      | Per-instance message override (ADR-0005).                                                 |
| `className`  | `string`               | none      | Merged with the component class.                                                          |

Other attributes and `ref` pass through to the element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `role="progressbar"` with no value (indeterminate) and an accessible name. It is **not** `role="status"` or `aria-live`: a screen reader does not announce every spinner when it mounts. One announcement strategy per screen: the button (`Button` announces pending and done) or a single status region you control.
- Decorative mode: `aria-hidden="true"`. Pair it with visible status text in a `role="status"` region, as in the `DecorativeWithText` story.
- Reduced motion: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the ring does not rotate. It stays as a static open ring; the accessible name and the busy control state carry the meaning.
- Forced colors: the ring is drawn with `currentColor` borders, which follow the system text color.
- Color: inherits the text color, so it needs no extra contrast treatment beyond its container's.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- The name is a short noun phrase in sentence case: "Loading", "Loading orders". No ellipsis, no exclamation mark.
- Default text comes from the `Spinner` message catalog (`en`: "Loading", `pt-BR`: "Carregando"). Override it per instance or through `DSProvider messages={{ Spinner: { loading: '...' } }}`.

sections.content:
```tsx

Saving changes

```

whenNotToUse: Choices confirmed later with a Save button or submitted as an agreement: `Checkbox`.

sections.heading: When not to use

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                                                  | Notes                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                               | Visible label. Without it pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (renders only the track).                          |
| `description`                                                         | Secondary text under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.                                 |
| `labelPlacement`                                                      | `start` (default): text on the leading side, track on the trailing side, spread across the row. `end`: track first. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)`             | React Aria naming.                                                                                                  |
| `name`, `value`                                                       | Submitted with the form while on (`value` defaults to `on`).                                                        |
| `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` | Standard states.                                                                                                    |

- Sizes come from component tokens: `--ds-switch-track-width`, `--ds-switch-track-height`, `--ds-switch-knob-size`, `--ds-switch-knob-offset`.
- The row is at least as tall as the track and the whole row is the click target, with one toggle per click.
- Reduced motion: transitions are removed by the base layer.
- Forced colors: the track gets a system border and a `Highlight` fill when on; the knob uses `CanvasText`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- `Space` toggles the focused switch. `Enter` does not toggle (it submits the form, as for any native checkbox).
- Announced as "switch, on/off", named by the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- State is conveyed by position and by color, and by the announced state.

```tsx

- Dimensions are component tokens; controlled props follow React Aria.

  Label

sections.heading: Props
sections.content:
`Tag`

| Prop         | Type                | Notes                                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`   | `ReactNode`         | The text                                                                      |
| `textValue`  | `string`            | Required when `children` is not a string: names the tag and its remove button |
| `id`         | `Key`               | In a group: the key. Standalone: the DOM id                                   |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean`           | Dashed border and reduced opacity; not removable or selectable                |
| `onRemove`   | `() => void`        | Standalone only: shows a remove button. In a group use the group's `onRemove` |
| `messages`   | `{ remove(label) }` | Per-instance override of the remove button name                               |

`TagGroup`

| Prop                                                                                        | Notes                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                                                     | Visible label. Without it set `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`  |
| `onRemove(keys: Set<Key>)`                                                                  | Enables removal: Backspace, Delete and the remove button call it |
| `selectionMode`, `selectedKeys`, `defaultSelectedKeys`, `onSelectionChange`, `disabledKeys` | React Aria selection API                                         |
| `items`, `children` (function)                                                              | Dynamic collections, as in React Aria                            |
| `renderEmptyState`                                                                          | Content shown when no tag is left ("No filters applied")         |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- A group is a `grid` with one `row` per tag. Arrow keys move between tags (roving focus); the focused tag is the only one in the tab order.
- **Backspace and Delete remove the focused tag** (or all selected tags) when the group has `onRemove`. Keyboard users are told so by a description that React Aria adds to the focused tag.
- **The remove button is named "Remove {text}"** from the message catalog (pt-BR: "Remover {text}"), not just "Remove". The button is also a tab stop after its tag, and is a 24 by 24 pixel target (WCAG 2.5.8).
- After a removal, focus moves to a neighbouring tag (React Aria); handle the empty state with `renderEmptyState` and move focus to something sensible yourself if the whole group disappears.
- Selection is exposed as `aria-selected`, and shown with the accent border and tint (a permitted use of the accent). Selection is never signalled by color alone: the state is announced.
- A standalone `Tag` is plain text. With `onRemove` it contains a real `<button>` (Enter or Space); Backspace and Delete do nothing there because the tag itself is not focusable. Use a `TagGroup` when keyboard removal matters.
- Text is `--ds-text-2` on the page surface; disabled tags are exempt from contrast and carry `aria-disabled`.

sections.heading: Content rules
sections.content:
- Short, lowercase or code-like values are fine (`v2.4.0`, `ORD-1048`); filters use the user's own words.
- Write a `textValue` that reads well after "Remove": "Remove linen".

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content:
```tsx
<Tag>v2.4.0</Tag>

<TagGroup label="Fabric" onRemove={(keys) => setTags((t) => t.filter((x) => !keys.has(x)))}>
  {tags.map((tag) => <Tag key={tag} id={tag}>{tag}</Tag>)}
</TagGroup>
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- The remove button name includes the tag text (it was a bare "Remover").
- 24 px target for the remove button; height, padding and button size are tokens (`--ds-tag-*`).
- `TagGroup` adds keyboard removal, roving focus, selection and an empty state.
- The "×" glyph is the bundled `X` icon, hidden from assistive technology.
- No `style` prop.

- The "×" glyph is the bundled `X` icon, hidden from assistive technology.

docs.summary: Multi-line text field. Same contract as [Input](../Input/Input.md) (label, description, error, states, validation timing from [Field](../Field/Field.md)), plus an aside, auto-growing height and a character count. Built on React Aria `TextField` + `TextArea`.
whenToUse: Notes, comments, descriptions, messages longer than a line.
whenNotToUse: One line of text: `Input`.
Rich text or Markdown editing: a dedicated editor.
keyboard: Keyboard: standard text editing; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Tab` leaves the field.

sections.heading: When to use
sections.content: - Notes, comments, descriptions, messages longer than a line.

sections.heading: When not to use
sections.content:
- One line of text: `Input`.
- Rich text or Markdown editing: a dedicated editor.

sections.heading: Props (key ones)
sections.content:
| Prop                                         | Notes                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`       | As in `Input`.                                                                                                           |
| `aside`                                      | Text on the label line, aligned to the end ("Optional", "Markdown supported"). Part of the description, not of the name. |
| `rows`                                       | Visible lines. Default 3.                                                                                                |
| `resize`                                     | `none`, `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, `both`.                                                                      |
| `autoGrow`                                   | Grows with its content; the manual resize handle is off.                                                                 |
| `maxLength` + `showCount`                    | Shows "used / max" on the label line and announces the remaining characters politely.                                    |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)` | React Aria naming; `onChange` receives the string.                                                                       |
| `textareaRef` / `ref`                        | `textareaRef` is the `<textarea>`, `ref` the field root.                                                                 |
| `messages`                                   | `count`, `remaining`, `over`, `requiredMark`.                                                                            |

sections.heading: Character count
sections.content:
- The visible counter ("12 / 200", formatted for the locale) is `aria-hidden`: announcing it on every keystroke would drown the user.
- A separate visually hidden `role="status"` (polite) region announces "N characters remaining" once typing has paused for one second. It stays silent until the value changes, and says "N characters over the limit" when a controlled value exceeds `maxLength`.
- Plural forms and the pt-BR text come from `Textarea.messages.ts`. Override `count`, `remaining` and `over` per instance or via `DSProvider messages={{ Textarea: { ... } }}`.
- `showCount` has no effect without `maxLength`. The native `maxLength` stops typing at the limit.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.content:
- Native `<textarea>` named by its label; `aside` and `description` are in `aria-describedby` (description first, then aside).
- Keyboard: standard text editing; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Tab` leaves the field.
- Auto-grow keeps all content visible (no inner scrollbar), which helps zoom and reflow.

sections.heading: Example
sections.content:
```tsx
<Textarea label="Notes" aside="Optional" description="Plain text only." maxLength={500} showCount />
<Textarea label="Message" autoGrow rows={2} isRequired errorMessage="Write a message." />
```

sections.heading: Differences from the handoff
sections.content:
- `aside` is associated with the field; it was a floating span.
- New: `autoGrow`, character count with a debounced polite announcement, read-only, shared validation timing.
- Focus styling is CSS and survives consumer `onFocus`/`onBlur`.
- `resize` accepts four values and is ignored with `autoGrow`.

Root provider of Loui DS. Supplies the locale (also to RAC through its

hooks.name: useControllableState
hooks.description:
Controlled/uncontrolled state for the `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`
convention (AGENTS.md section 9). Thin wrapper over react-stately's `useControlledState`,
which also warns in development when a component switches between modes.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useControllableState({ value: props.value, defaultValue: props.defaultValue ?? '', onChange: props.onValueChange });
```
hooks.signature: useControllableState<T>({ value, defaultValue, onChange, }: UseControllableStateOptions<T>): [T, (value: T) => void]

hooks.name: useDSLocale
hooks.description: Returns the active locale (BCP 47 tag) set by `DSProvider`; `en-US` without a provider.

hooks.name: useHotkey
hooks.description:
Runs `handler` when a single key combo is pressed.

- `combo`: modifiers joined with `+` and one key, e.g. `Mod+K`, `Shift+/`, `Alt+N`, `Escape`.
  `Mod` is Command on macOS and Control elsewhere.
- Ignores events from editable fields (unless `allowInEditable`), IME composition,
  key auto-repeat (unless `allowRepeat`) and events another handler already prevented.

This is deliberately small. A shortcut registry with conflict detection and a help
overlay is a separate task (GAP-004).
hooks.signature: useHotkey(combo: string, handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void, { enabled, scope, allowInEditable, allowRepeat, preventDefault, platform, }?: UseHotkeyOptions): void

hooks.name: useMediaQuery
hooks.description:
Subscribes to a CSS media query. SSR-safe: on the server (and during hydration)
it returns `defaultValue` (`false` unless given), then the real value after hydration.

Prefer CSS media queries for styling; use this only when behavior (not appearance) depends on the query.

utilities.signature: compareText(a: string, b: string, locale: string): number

utilities.name: contrastRatio
utilities.description: WCAG contrast ratio between two hex colors, from `1` (identical) to `21` (black on white). Order does not matter.

utilities.name: createTextCollator
utilities.description:
Collator for alphabetical order as the product requires (AGENTS.md section 5, rule 5b):
accent- and case-insensitive (`sensitivity: 'base'`) with natural number order
(`numeric: true`, so `Item 2` sorts before `Item 10`). The instance is shared
and cached per locale; do not mutate it.

utilities.name: daysBetween
utilities.description:
Whole days from `isoA` to `isoB` (positive when `isoB` is later). Uses UTC
date math, so daylight-saving changes cannot produce 23- or 25-hour "days".
Invalid input throws in development and returns `NaN` in production.

Declares a component's catalog. Identity function that type-checks that
`pt-BR` has exactly the same keys and signatures as `en`.

utilities.name: dueStatus
utilities.description:
Urgency of a due date: overdue (`< 0` days) is `danger`, due within a week
(`0` to `7`) is `warning`, later is `neutral`. The visible text always comes
from messages (color is never the only signal, AGENTS.md section 5).

utilities.name: formatCurrency
utilities.description:
Formats money held as an integer in minor units (ADR-0006):
`formatCurrency(123456, 'USD', 'en-US')` is `$1,234.56`.

The amount is passed to `Intl` as an exact decimal string, so there is no
floating-point drift. Non-integer or unsafe amounts throw in development
(a sign of a unit bug at the call site) and are rounded in production.
utilities.signature: formatCurrency(minorUnits: number, currency: string, locale: string, options?: FormatCurrencyOptions): string

utilities.name: formatDate
utilities.description:
Formats an ISO date for `locale`. Formatting happens in UTC, so the day never
shifts with the viewer's time zone. Invalid input throws in development and
is returned unchanged in production.

`formatDate('2026-10-31', 'en-US', 'medium')` is `Oct 31, 2026`.
utilities.signature: formatDate(iso: ISODate, locale: string, style?: DateStyle): string

utilities.name: formatNumber
utilities.description: Formats a decimal number for `locale` (`1234.5` becomes `1,234.5` in `en-US`).
utilities.signature: formatNumber(value: number, locale: string, options?: FormatNumberOptions): string

utilities.name: formatPercent
utilities.description:
Formats a ratio as a percentage: `0.256` becomes `26%` in `en-US`.
Pass `maximumFractionDigits` for more precision.
utilities.signature: formatPercent(ratio: number, locale: string, options?: Omit<FormatNumberOptions, "unit" | "unitDisplay">): string

utilities.name: formatRelativeDays
utilities.description:
Relative day label from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: 'auto'`:
`-1` is `yesterday`, `0` is `today`, `1` is `tomorrow`, `3` is `in 3 days`.
`days` must be an integer (throws in development, rounded in production).

utilities.name: getCurrencyDigits
utilities.description:
Number of minor-unit digits of a currency (2 for USD/BRL, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD),
read from `Intl` so we never keep our own table.

utilities.name: getInitials
utilities.description:
Initials of a person's name: the first letter of the first and of the last word
(`Ana Maria da Silva` gives `AS`), or one letter for a single word. Uses `Intl.Segmenter`,
so combined characters stay whole, and upper-cases with the locale rules (`i` in `tr`).

utilities.name: highlightMatch
utilities.description:
Splits `text` into matched and unmatched segments for highlighting, ignoring case
and accents. The segments always concatenate back to `text` exactly, and a match
keeps any combining marks attached to its last letter. All occurrences are returned.

`highlightMatch('Crème brûlée', 'creme')` gives `[{ text: 'Crème', match: true }, { text: ' brûlée', match: false }]`.

utilities.name: isISODate
utilities.description: True if `value` is a real calendar date written as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

utilities.name: matchesSearch
utilities.description: True when `text` contains `query`, ignoring case and accents. An empty query matches everything.

utilities.name: normalizeSearch
utilities.description:
Normalizes text for accent- and case-insensitive search: `Café` and `cafe` both
become `cafe`. Works per code point so it stays index-aligned with `highlightMatch`.

utilities.name: parseCurrencyInput
utilities.description:
Parses what the user typed in a currency field into integer minor units, using
the digits-only typing model: every digit shifts in from the right, and any
other character (separators, symbols, spaces, a sign) is ignored. Typing
`1`, `2`, `3` into a USD field yields `1`, `12`, `123`, shown as `$0.01`,
`$0.12`, `$1.23`. Digits of the locale's numbering system (e.g. Arabic-Indic)
and full-width digits count as digits. Empty input is `0`. Input longer than
15 digits is cut, so the result is always a safe integer.

`currency` is validated through `Intl` (throws `RangeError` for an invalid code).
Pasting `12` into a USD field means `$0.12` by this model; callers that want
to accept pasted decimals must handle paste before calling this function.
utilities.signature: parseCurrencyInput(text: string, currency: string, locale: string): number

utilities.name: plural
utilities.description:
Picks a plural form for `count` using `Intl.PluralRules`.
Call it from catalog functions, passing that catalog's own locale:
`selected: (n: number) => plural('en', n, { one: '1 selected', other: `${n} selected` })`.
utilities.signature: plural(locale: string, count: number, forms: PluralForms): string

utilities.name: readableTextOn
utilities.description:
Which text color is more readable on a background color: `'light'` (white-ish
text, for dark backgrounds) or `'dark'`. Picks whichever of white or black has
the higher WCAG contrast, replacing the handoff's 0.299/0.587/0.114 shortcut.

utilities.name: relativeLuminance
utilities.description:
WCAG 2.x relative luminance of a hex color: `0` (black) to `1` (white).
Accepts `#rgb` and `#rrggbb`. Invalid colors throw in development and count as black in production.

utilities.name: sortByText
utilities.description:
Returns a new array sorted alphabetically by `getText(item)`. Stable: items whose
text compares equal (for example `Ana` and `ana`, or `é` and `e`) keep their input order.
utilities.signature: sortByText<T>(items: readonly T[], getText: (item: T) => string, locale: string): T[]

utilities.name: SUPPORTED_LOCALES
utilities.description: Locales that ship with built-in message catalogs (ADR-0005).

utilities.name: toISODate
utilities.description:
Converts a `Date` to `YYYY-MM-DD` using its **local** calendar day (what the
user sees on their clock). Pass `{ utc: true }` to use the UTC day instead.
Invalid dates and years outside 0000-9999 throw in development and give `''` in production.
utilities.signature: toISODate(date: Date, options?: { utc?: boolean; }): ISODate

utilities.name: warnDeprecated
utilities.description:
Logs a deprecation warning once per `name`. Development only: a no-op in
production builds and on the server-side of production. Call it from the
deprecated component's body or module, passing what to use instead.

`warnDeprecated('OldButton', 'Use Button with variant="ghost" instead.')`
